category_title: Adolescent students with learning disabilities who under-request accommodations and struggle with the social steps of self-advocacy
minimal_context: The student is completing a Skills Inventory Survey in a special education English class to identify their strengths and needs.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please complete this Skills Inventory Survey so we can identify your strengths and needs, and figure out what accommodations you might need.

STUDENT: I don't think I will ever need an accommodation. I've never requested one.

TUTOR: Let's just go through the list of skills on the survey.

STUDENT: I don't even know what an LD is or that I have this learning condition.

TUTOR: What do you think should happen with your accommodations?

STUDENT: I expect my teachers to be responsible for my accommodations. I have little to do with them.

options.A: Share baseline data with the student and discuss how their grades could improve with appropriately requested accommodations.
options.B: Have the student use a note-taking app to take notes, organize their work, and archive past surveys.
options.C: Offer the choice of visiting with a preferred teacher contingent upon meeting a daily survey completion goal.
options.D: Divide the inventory survey into small parts, each of which is completed by a different group member.
